name: Vine Density Calculator
seoDesc: Vine density — vines per hectare — is set by row spacing and vine spacing, and it drives competition, fruit exposure and yield per vine. Free vine density cal
summary:
Vine density — vines per hectare — is set by row spacing and vine spacing, and it drives competition, fruit exposure and yield per vine. It returns vines per hectare, vines per 100 m of row, yield per vine and grams per bunch, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator gives density, vines per row, and the yield per vine that a target tonnes-per-hectare implies. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Vine Density
sections.html:
Vines/ha = 10 000 ÷ (row spacing × vine spacing); kg per vine = yield ÷ density

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
row spacingdistance between rowsm
vine spacingdistance between vines in the rowm
densityvines per hectarevines/ha

sections.title: How do I use the Vine Density?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: row spacing of 2.5 m, vine spacing of 1.2 m, target yield of 8 t/ha, bunches per vine of 24.

Substituting them into the formula gives vines per hectare of 3,333.33 vines/ha, vines per 100 m of row of 83.33 vines, yield per vine of 2.4 kg, grams per bunch of 100 g.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 3 000Low densitybush vines, old-vine plots, dry-grown
3 000 – 6 000Typicalmost modern trellised vineyards
above 7 000High densitycool-climate quality plantings

  • Doubling density roughly halves the yield per vine for the same tonnes per hectare, which changes fruit composition as much as it changes tonnage.

  • Row spacing also has to fit the tractor: 2.0–2.5 m is common because machinery sets a floor.

  • Bunch weight is the least stable variable in the chain — it moves by 30% between seasons.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Using feet for spacing in a metre-based formula.
  • Setting density from yield targets alone, ignoring vine vigour and water supply.
  • Confusing tonnes per hectare with tonnes per acre (1 t/ac ≈ 2.47 t/ha).

faq.q: How many vines per hectare at 2.5 × 1.2 m?
Does higher density give better wine?
faq.a: It can improve competition and fruit exposure, but only where water and nutrition allow it.

faq.q: What does the Vine Density actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns vines per hectare, vines per 100 m of row, yield per vine and grams per bunch. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
